newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran resistance rallies in Germany against Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Iran resistance rallies in Germany against Tehran.

text.p: Thousands of opponents of Iran's Moslem rulers rallied in Germany on Friday, calling on the international community to slap economic sanctions on Tehran and break off diplomatic relations.
Waving flags and shouting slogans, a crowd of around 10,000 listened to a speech by Iranian resistance leader Maryam Rajavi, which organisers said was being relayed live from the Iran-Iraq border.
"Trampling upon the people's sovereignty, exporting terrorism and practising misogyny are embedded in the nature and constitution of this regime," Rajavi said.
Parallel rallies were also scheduled to take place in Sweden and on the fringes of the Denver summit of the Group of Seven industrialised nations.
Marzieh, the diva of Iranian music known as the nightingale of Persia, and Miriam Makeba, the South African singer and former anti-aparteid campaigner, were among the performers at the rally.

The exiled resistance movement on Thursday criticised Juergen Moellemann, a parliamentary deputy with the Free Democrats and regarded as a maverick in Bonn, for trying to patch up relations with Tehran on a visit last weekend.
The Free Democrats are the junior partner in the coalition government.

European Union (EU) states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after a German court concluded in April that Iran's top leaders had ordered the 1992 assassination of a Kurdish-Iranian dissident in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in the killings.
